overview: Despatch reports Dairen postal officials rejected an American firm's China-bound letters for not being in Japanese; Grummon protested to Communications Bureau chief Ito, citing the 1911 treaty, and Ito denied authorizing it though evidence suggested his own bureau originated the restriction.

subfiles.title: Despatch on attempted interference with an American firm’s mail to China
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports and protests the Dairen postal authorities’ refusal to accept correspondence sent by an American business representative to his firm’s office in Tientsin.
subfiles.summary: Dairen postal workers refused Fraser Federal's October 1937 letters to Tientsin for not being in Japanese; Grummon cited the 1911 treaty, and Bureau chief Ito denied any ban and ordered correction, though evidence suggested his own bureau issued the restrictive notice.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911

interest: Shows American diplomatic pushback against Dairen postal interference with mail to China under treaty rights.
